“There has been a narrative that the United States is out of the foreign assistance business. Nothing could be further from the truth. We are going to spend much more in the Indo-Pacific over the coming years than we ever have before. And we’re going to spend it in different ways. It’s going to be about private sector growth. It’s going to be about catalytic investment.”

So begins this 29 December press release from @StateDept , Bureau of Asian and Pacific Affairs. The approach moves away from the old narrative that aid = influence, implicit in work like @LowyInstitute Pacific aid map and, if it works, reflects what many in the region have been calling for over the years, trade and sustainable development, rather than just aid.

Some of what's announced are legacy (South Pacific Tuna Treaty funding) but other announcements indicate a new focus, including embedding the fight against transnational crime (crime leads to corruption pathways that additional Chinese political warfare operations can flow through).

Apart from what has just been announced for Palau (https://t.co/wh1pG3ZljV), according to the release, the "Department is supporting new joint law enforcement initiatives to counter the trafficking and production of synthetic drugs and precursor chemicals and programs to combat online scam operations responsible for the theft of billions of dollars from U.S citizens."

Other excerpts:

* State Department is working with the United States Trade Development Agency (@USTDA ) to seed private sector development of American-led airport infrastructure at the Koror International Airport in Palau.

* The U.S. plans to work with Taiwan to rebuild the Nitijela, the Republic of the #MarshallIslands’ parliament building, after a recent fire. The United States and #Taiwan are also working together to help replace Air Marshall Islands’ fleet and provide disaster relief capacity and connectivity to outer islands.

* #Australia and the United States are continuing to partner with #PapuaNewGuinea on economic development in the industrial and port hub of Lae, which includes new planned support from the United States to bolster cargo inspection and screening infrastructure and training to enhance port security, disrupt transnational criminal activity, and spur economic development.

There are also new initiatives for #Philippines (which I think of as an honorary Pacific Island) on health, energy, responsible fishing, and private sector-led investment in the Luzon Economic Corridor.

State seems to be serious about how to block Chinese illegal, coercive, aggressive and deceptive activity in the Pacific Islands, while building resilience.  It won't be easy, but it looks like they are going to try.

https://t.co/4TqsAP0CUC
